**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Persist the automatically selected strip's ID**

If the panel initially receives strips `[A, B]`, A appears selected but `selectedId` remains `undefined` until the user explicitly selects a strip. Restarting the engine with `[B, A]` therefore selects B, even though A is still declared, contrary to the documented reconnect behavior. Subsequent effect choices then target B rather than the previously selected strip. Store the resolved selection's ID when selecting the initial or fallback strip, while preserving it during disconnection.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Ignore non-primary pointer buttons when choosing effects**

Right-clicking or middle-clicking an enabled effect button currently calls `choose` and sends a PUT, because `pointerdown` fires for those buttons too. Opening the browser context menu can consequently change the live lighting effect without a normal activation. Filter pointer events to the primary button before choosing the effect, while retaining touch and keyboard activation.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Hecho en 16ccb4c: `pointerdown` solo elige con el botón principal (`button` 0, que es también el del dedo y el lápiz). Los botones central y derecho ya no cambian el efecto, y el teclado sigue igual. Lleva un test por cada botón.

Hecho en e0db936: `App` guarda el `id` de la tira que se selecciona sola (la primera al abrir, o la primera si falta la elegida), ajustando el estado durante el render. Así, si el motor vuelve con las tiras en otro orden, sigue seleccionada la misma. Sin conexión no hay tiras, y la selección se conserva. Lleva su test con las tiras en orden inverso.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Wait for the breathing frame before snapshotting the timeline**

If the effect-state update reaches the page before the next frame tick, both `aria-current` assertions can pass while the timeline still contains no breathing frame. The engine broadcasts the strip-state update synchronously through `strips.watch` (`packages/engine/src/adapters/server.ts:273–275`), whereas frames are broadcast separately by `viewerOutput.write`. Taking a one-time snapshot here can therefore trigger “La tira no ha pintado la respiración” even when the switch completes within 100 ms. Wait for a matching frame before reading the timeline, and continue using its recorded arrival timestamp for the latency assertion.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Hecho en 38b0f77: el test espera, con `expect.poll`, a que llegue un frame de la respiración posterior a la pulsación, y después lee los tiempos. La latencia sigue saliendo del instante de llegada de ese frame. Tres ejecuciones seguidas en verde (27,6, 36,3 y 35,9 ms).
